October: Autumn's Grand Finale

October delivers the UK's most colourful landscapes. Deciduous woodlands blaze with red, gold, and copper. Bracken turns the hillsides rust-orange. The light is low and golden. For riding, October demands more preparation than summer months but rewards the effort with scenery at its most dramatic.

Conditions

  • Temperature: Average 8-14°C. First frosts possible inland by late October.
  • Daylight: Clocks go back at the end of October, losing an evening hour. Sunrise 7am, sunset 5:30pm (before change).
  • Weather: Variable. Beautiful clear days alternate with autumn storms. Check forecasts daily and be flexible.

October Highlights

  • Peak autumn colour: Mid to late October sees the most spectacular tree colours. The New Forest, Wye Valley, Perthshire, and Lake District are exceptional.
  • Deer rutting: Red deer stags roar and clash antlers through October. Richmond Park, Exmoor, and the Scottish Highlands are the best watching spots — and all require caution on roads near deer populations.
  • Empty roads: Tourism is minimal. Popular areas are deserted compared to summer. Roads feel private.

October Riding Adjustments

  • Warm layers: Mornings can be cold. Carry an extra thermal layer and gloves.
  • Wet leaves: The biggest hazard of autumn riding. Wet leaves on tarmac are as slippery as ice. Be especially cautious on tree-lined roads and in villages.
  • Low sun: The low October sun can cause blinding glare in early morning and late afternoon. Carry a tinted and clear visor.
  • Reduced grip: Cooler tarmac means slightly less tyre grip. Allow extra braking distance.
An October ride through the Perthshire Big Tree Country or the Wye Valley with autumn colours at their peak is one of the finest visual experiences British motorcycling offers. Worth the cold hands.

October Tour Ideas

A long weekend in Perthshire during October's peak autumn colour is outstanding. The roads through Glen Lyon, around Loch Tummel, and through the forests around Pitlochry pass some of the most colourful landscapes in Britain. The Enchanted Forest light show at Faskally Wood adds an evening attraction.

In England, the Wye Valley and Forest of Dean combine autumn colour with atmospheric gorge and forest riding. The A466 through the lower Wye Valley, with beech and oak woodland blazing on both sides of the river gorge, is one of the most beautiful road rides in Britain during mid-October.

Bike Preparation for Shorter Days

October demands attention to lighting. With sunset before 6pm by month's end, evening riding in reduced light is likely. Ensure all lights are clean and working, carry a clear visor for dusk riding, and consider high-visibility clothing. Reflective elements on your gear become more important as the days shorten — other road users need to see you in the gloom of an October afternoon.

October is also time for an autumn maintenance check. Inspect chain wear and tension, check brake pad thickness, and top up fluids before the cold weather arrives. A bike that enters winter well-maintained emerges in spring ready to ride rather than needing urgent work when the season begins. faq.q: What is riding like in October?
faq.a: October delivers Britain's most colourful landscapes, with deciduous woodlands blazing red, gold and copper and bracken turning hillsides rust-orange under a low, golden sun. Temperatures average 8-14C with first frosts possible inland late in the month, and the weather is variable, so beautiful clear days alternate with autumn storms. It demands more preparation than summer but rewards the effort.

faq.q: Why are wet leaves so dangerous in October?
faq.a: Wet leaves on tarmac are the biggest hazard of autumn riding and are as slippery as ice. Be especially cautious on tree-lined roads and in villages where leaves accumulate. Combine this with cooler tarmac reducing tyre grip and you should allow extra braking distance and ride smoothly. The low October sun also causes blinding glare in early morning and late afternoon.

faq.q: Where are the best autumn-colour routes in October?
faq.a: Perthshire's Big Tree Country is Scotland's showpiece, with roads through Glen Lyon, around Loch Tummel and near Pitlochry, plus the Enchanted Forest light show at Faskally Wood. In England, the Wye Valley and Forest of Dean combine colour with gorge and forest riding, and the A466 through the lower Wye Valley forms a golden tunnel of beech and oak in mid-October.

faq.q: What is deer rutting and why does it matter?
faq.a: Red deer stags roar and clash antlers through October, and Richmond Park, Exmoor and the Scottish Highlands are the best watching spots. It matters for riders because it means increased deer activity near roads in these areas, so ride with extra caution. A deer strike at speed is serious, so slow down and stay alert on roads through deer country, especially at dawn and dusk.

faq.q: How should I prepare my bike for October's shorter days?
faq.a: With sunset before 6pm by month's end, evening riding in reduced light is likely, so ensure all lights are clean and working, carry a clear visor for dusk and add reflective or high-visibility clothing. October is also time for an autumn maintenance check: inspect chain wear and tension, check brake pad thickness and top up fluids so the bike enters winter well-maintained.
